entities.summary:
Pietro Ungarello di Marco de' Natali, better known as Petrus de Natalibus, was an Italian bishop and the author of a collection of lives of the saints. Born in unknown, de Natalibus served as the bishop of Brixia (modern-day Brescia) from 1378 to 1406. During his tenure, he implemented various reforms aimed at improving the lives of the poor and the clergy. His work on the lives of saints has had a lasting impact on the development of hagiography in the Catholic Church.

De Natalibus was a key figure in the Counter-Reformation, and his writings were widely read and studied by theologians and clerics during the 15th and 16th centuries. His influence can still be seen in the modern-day Catholic Church's approach to hagiography and its emphasis on the importance of saints' lives in shaping Christian doctrine.

One of de Natalibus' most notable achievements was his role in the Council of Trent, where he contributed to the development of the Church's catechetical program. His work on the lives of saints helped to shape the Church's understanding of its saints and their role in the Christian faith.

In conclusion, Petrus de Natalibus' contributions to the development of hagiography and his role in the Counter-Reformation make him a significant figure in the history of the Catholic Church.

The legacy of de Natalibus can be seen in the many lives of saints that he wrote, which continue to be studied and revered by Catholics around the world. His work has had a lasting impact on the Church's approach to hagiography and its emphasis on the importance of saints' lives in shaping Christian doctrine.
